blocks.heading: Unified Role-Based Access Control for Digital Experience

blocks.text: The Digital Experience (ZDX) Role supports Unified Role-Based Access Control (RBAC). Administrators can now view, create, and manage ZDX roles centrally on the Role Management page (Administration > Role Management > Role Management).
See image.
The existing ZDX Role Management page is deprecated if you use Unified RBAC.
To learn more, see About Role Management and Adding ZDX Roles.

blocks.text: You can select a specific TCP traceroute when you configure a Cloud Path probe:

blocks.item: Resilient TCP Type: Traceroute when the TCP connection fails and then retries using the Conventional TCP type.
Strict TCP Type: Traceroute when the TCP connection fails and there are no other connections to fall back to.

blocks.text: The Conventional TCP type is the original TCP traceroute based on sync (SYN) packets and is potentially blocked by firewalls.

Any probe configured with a TCP type prior to this enhancement defaults to a Resilient TCP type configuration. If you want to continue using the Conventional TCP type, configure your existing probe to select Conventional TCP Type.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring a Probe and Supported Versions & Feature Compatibility.

The Network Intelligence dashboard has the following enhancements:

blocks.item: Alternative views for User Experience & Network Insights: Configure your views to display the metrics for User Experience & Network Insights based on the top 5 ISPs with the highest number of probes.
You can also view the historical comparison between different times or view geographical comparison between different locations.

Zscaler Experience Center simplifies Zero Trust adoption and operations through an intuitive, unified admin experience in the Zscaler Admin Console. Digital Experience (ZDX) is available in the Experience Center and delivers a horizontal platform experience across multiple tenants.
See image.
To learn more, see What is Zscaler Experience Center and Upgrading to Zscaler Experience Center.

Real User Monitoring captures and analyzes user interactions with applications through their web browsers to create a comprehensive visibility into the application's digital experience. You can use Real User Monitoring to identify bottlenecks a user might encounter while they are accessing configured applications through their web browsers.
See image.
To learn more, see Understanding Real User Monitoring and Evaluating Application Details.
The ZDX API includes the following endpoints:

blocks.item: /snapshot/alert: Share a ZDX Snapshot for a given alert ID to evaluate alert details.
/snapshot/user: Share a ZDX Snapshot for a given user ID to monitor user details about device and application use.

blocks.text: To learn more, see ZDX Snapshots.

blocks.heading: Zoom Call Quality Monitoring Exclusion Criteria

blocks.text: Call Quality Monitoring for Zoom now supports exclusion criteria during tenant onboarding, allowing the collection of call quality data for all users except specified users or groups.
New fields in the Monitoring Criteria section:

blocks.item: User groups: Select one or more groups to exclude from monitoring.
Users: Add individual users to exclude.
Departments: Exclude entire departments to streamline administration.

blocks.text: These options make it easy to apply broad monitoring while exempting specific users or teams as needed.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring Zoom Call Quality for Digital Experience Monitoring.

ZDX logs and data are now stored in Canada in addition to the United States, the European Union (Western Europe, Netherlands), Singapore or Australia East (New South Wales). Contact your Zscaler Account team for details.
To learn more about Zscaler's retention of logs and data, see ZDX Logs.
ZDX now supports IPv6 to include dual-stack (IPv4 and IPv6) or IPv6-only configurations.

ZDX IPv6 visibility requires Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA) IPv6 to be enabled, as ZDX relies on ZIA to route and inspect IPv6 traffic for telemetry collection. To learn more, see Understanding IPv6 Support.
You can view IPv6 configurations across the ZDX Admin Portal (e.g., Cloud Path, Device Details).
See image.
To learn more, see Viewing IPv6 Configurations.
